key_evidence_spans: A 56-year-old Caucasian man presented in mid-winter with a 2-week history of tingling and burning of both feet
He noted bluish discoloration, swelling, and some blistering on the dorsum of his toes
He reported a lifelong history of “white-attacks” of his fingers when cold (consistent with Raynaud’s phenomenon)
The remainder of a hypercoagulable and vasculitic work-up, including cryoglobulins and ANCA panels, was negative
